title: 2D Morton Code Bit Interleaving
description: Given two 16-bit non-negative integers `x` and `y` (`0 <= x, y <= 65535`), compute their 32-bit unsigned 2D Morton code (Z-order curve index) by interleaving their binary bits: bit `i` of `x` is placed at bit `2 * i`, and bit `i` of `y` is placed at bit `2 * i + 1` for `0 <= i < 16`. Return the resulting unsigned 32-bit value as a non-negative 64-bit integer.
hints: Spread the 16 bits of a coordinate into even bit positions using four parallel divide-and-conquer shift-and-mask rounds with masks `0x00FF00FF`, `0x0F0F0F0F`, `0x33333333`, and `0x55555555`.
Combine the spread coordinates via `spread(x) | (spread(y) << 1)` in 64-bit arithmetic so bit 31 never turns negative.

examples.explanation: x = 1 (01) places bits at even positions (0001) and y = 2 (10) places bits at odd positions (1000), giving 1001 = 9.
x = 5 (101) spreads to 10001 = 17, and y = 0 contributes 0.
